nodes.label: Since 2014, recurrent abscesses, indurated erythematous plaques, and sclerosis on both upper legs
56-year-old woman with medical history of hypermobility syndrome diagnosed in 1998 and cosmetic breast augmentation surgery in 2002
Progressive chronic fatigue and joint pain over years without definitive diagnosis despite multiple specialist consultations; no symptoms of autoinflammation or autoimmunity besides periodic fever
Physical examination revealed indurated erythematous plaques, sclerosis, and abscesses on both upper legs; no other significant physical findings noted
Skin biopsy shows granulomatous and lymphoplasmacytic inflammation, septal/fascial sclerosis, and histiocytic fibrosis
Recurrent bacterial skin abscesses (Staphylococcus aureus infection)
Skin biopsy shows histiocytic MORO-positive particles
Wound culture, special stains, and immunologic workup have not yet been performed
